name: Dead Aim
author: gytdoo
description: Deadlocked-style controls and camera for Going Commando: lock-strafe, remappable shoulder buttons, a free camera for the stick, mouse and gyro, aiming on the move, each weapon's own crosshair, aim assist and Auto Gadgets. Settings: Pause > Options > Dead Aim.

conflicts.reason: both change what the shoulder buttons and Fire do
both move the follow camera and hold L2
both turn the camera from Steam Input's gyro and trackpad
the board rides on the shoulder buttons Dead Aim remaps, and both move the camera

settings.name: Lock strafe
settings.description: Keeps Ratchet's back to the camera: never, while a weapon is out, or always. A Toggle strafe button flips it while held.

settings.name: Crouch behavior
settings.description: Standard: Crouch stops a running Ratchet. Deadlocked: held on the run it never stops him; with Jump he long jumps from the run, and with Square he tosses the wrench as he runs (the wrench in hand). Joe Wrench: as Deadlocked, and the toss works in the air too.

settings.name: L1
settings.description: What L1 does as Ratchet.

settings.name: L2
settings.description: What L2 does as Ratchet.

settings.name: R1
settings.description: What R1 does as Ratchet.

settings.name: R2
settings.description: What R2 does as Ratchet.

settings.name: Auto Gadgets
settings.description: Fire at a gadget's target puts the gadget in hand and uses it, then gives your weapon back: the Swingshot at the node you look at; All adds the Dynamo at its activators, the Tractor Beam at what it can carry, the Thermanator at pools and ice and the Hypnomatic at Receiver Bots.

settings.name: Camera
settings.description: Modern: a free camera for the stick, mouse and gyro that stays where you point it, keeps out of walls and aims where you look. Classic: the game's own camera and aim.

settings.name: Aim control
settings.description: Modern camera. Free Movement: holding Aim switches to the other view and you keep moving: first person, or, if you play with the game's first-person option on, the third-person camera and its crosshair. Standard: stand still to aim.

settings.name: Crosshair
settings.description: Modern camera: the size of the weapon's crosshair in third and first person (target markers keep theirs). Off: no crosshair in third person; first person keeps the game's own reticle.

settings.name: Camera speed
settings.description: How fast the right stick turns the Modern camera, at one of Deadlocked's speeds. Holding the stick fully sideways turns faster. Classic uses the game's own speed (Options > Camera).

settings.name: Vertical sensitivity
settings.description: How fast the right stick turns the Modern camera on the vertical axis, against the horizontal (which Camera speed sets): Deadlocked's (two-thirds), Up Your Arsenal's (a third faster), or Custom.

settings.name: Custom sensitivity
settings.description: With Vertical sensitivity on Custom: the vertical speed as a share of the horizontal (0.7 is about Deadlocked's).

settings.name: Aim assist
settings.description: With a weapon in hand, near an enemy the right stick slows and the view follows it while you move: Deadlocked's (20 degrees, 45 units) or Up Your Arsenal's (15 degrees, 30 units). The mouse and gyro are never slowed.

settings.name: Left click
settings.description: What the left mouse button does as Ratchet. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Right click
settings.description: What the right mouse button does as Ratchet. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Middle click
settings.description: What the middle mouse button does as Ratchet. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Mouse camera
settings.description: Turn the camera with the mouse. The cursor is held in the game's window while this is on or a mouse button does something. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Mouse sensitivity
settings.description: How fast the mouse turns the camera. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Invert Y
settings.description: Reverse the vertical axis. Older OpenRAC builds only, not on Android; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Gyro camera
settings.description: Turn the camera by moving the controller, through OpenRAC's own gyro filter: a DualSense, DualShock 4, Switch Pro Controller, Joy-Con or Steam Deck, on Linux (third-party Switch pads send no motion on these builds). Older OpenRAC builds on Linux only; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Gyro sensitivity
settings.description: How far the camera turns for the controller's turn (1: as far; 2, OpenRAC's default: twice as far). Older OpenRAC builds on Linux only; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Gyro turn with
settings.description: Which of the controller's turns turn the camera, as OpenRAC's own gyro has it: Player, its turn about the way up however it is held; Yaw, its twist held flat; Roll, leaning it like a wheel; Local, both twist and lean. Older OpenRAC builds on Linux only; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Gyro invert X
settings.description: Reverse the horizontal axis. Older OpenRAC builds on Linux only; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).

settings.name: Gyro invert Y
settings.description: Reverse the vertical axis. Older OpenRAC builds on Linux only; newer ones use OpenRAC's own settings (` or Start + Select).
